### Implementation Brief for Harborlight Tool Library

#### Introduction
Harborlight Tool Library aims to streamline the management of tools, ensuring safety, accessibility, and efficiency. The library will implement a robust system to handle tool intake, testing, and maintenance. The intake process will use the amber intake label to identify tools, ensuring quick access for users. Safety is paramount, with every high-risk tool requiring two people for testing to prevent accidents. A weekly safety review on Wednesdays will ensure ongoing compliance with safety protocols.

#### Access Workflow
The access workflow for Harborlight Tool Library will be streamlined to enhance user convenience and safety. Users will be required to present a valid ID at the library entrance to access the tools. Upon entry, they will be directed to the intake counter where the amber intake label will be applied to each tool. Tools will be categorized based on their risk level, with high-risk tools requiring additional testing procedures. Users will be provided with a tool card that includes the tool's name, description, and safety instructions. The card will also indicate the number of users allowed to borrow the tool at any given time to prevent overuse.

#### Volunteer Handover
To ensure a smooth transition of tools between volunteers, a volunteer handover system will be implemented. Each volunteer will be issued a tool logbook that records the tools they have borrowed and returned. The logbook will be checked by a supervisor before the volunteer leaves the library. This system will help in tracking the status of tools and ensure that no tools are left unattended or misused. Additionally, a weekly safety review will be conducted by the supervisor to discuss any issues or concerns with the tools and ensure that all safety protocols are followed.

#### Maintenance
Regular maintenance of tools is crucial to ensure their longevity and safety. Harborlight Tool Library will schedule maintenance checks for all tools every six months. Tools will be inspected for wear and tear, and any necessary repairs or replacements will be made. The maintenance schedule will be communicated to users through the tool cards, ensuring they are aware of when their tools will be checked. Additionally, a maintenance log will be kept in the library to record all maintenance activities and ensure that no tools are overlooked.

#### Concrete Monthly Maintenance Calendar
Harborlight Tool Library will maintain a monthly maintenance calendar to ensure all tools are checked and serviced regularly. The calendar will include specific dates for each tool category, such as high-risk tools, standard tools, and maintenance-free tools. For high-risk tools, maintenance checks will be conducted every six months, with two-person tests scheduled on the first Wednesday of each month. Standard tools will be checked every three months, and maintenance-free tools will be checked annually. This schedule ensures that all tools are serviced and tested regularly, maintaining their safety and functionality.

#### Worked Example of Two-Person Test
A worked example of the two-person test for high-risk tools is as follows: Suppose a user borrows a power saw from Harborlight Tool Library. The user will present the power saw to the intake counter, where the amber intake label is applied. The user will then be directed to the testing area, where two people will conduct the test. One person will operate the power saw, while the other will ensure safety protocols are followed, such as wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and checking for any malfunctions. After the test, both individuals will sign the tool logbook to confirm that the power saw is safe to use. This two-person test ensures that no single person is responsible for operating the tool, reducing the risk of accidents and ensuring compliance with safety protocols.

### Changes in Our Plan

Safety reviews for Harborlight Tool Library have been adjusted to occur every Friday instead of Wednesday. This change ensures that safety protocols are continuously monitored and updated as needed. Additionally, the intake label for tools has been changed from amber to teal, reflecting a shift in the color scheme used for tool identification. The teal label will help in distinguishing tools more clearly and making the intake process more efficient.

### Volunteer Update

1. **Tool Logbook**: Each volunteer will receive a tool logbook to record the tools they have borrowed and returned. This logbook will be checked by a supervisor before the volunteer leaves the library to ensure no tools are left unattended or misused.

2. **Weekly Safety Review**: A weekly safety review will be conducted by the supervisor on Fridays to discuss any issues or concerns with the tools and ensure that all safety protocols are followed.

3. **Maintenance Schedule**: Harborlight Tool Library will schedule maintenance checks for all tools every six months. Tools will be inspected for wear and tear, and any necessary repairs or replacements will be made. The maintenance schedule will be communicated to users through the tool cards, ensuring they are aware of when their tools will be checked.

4. **Safety Training**: Users will be trained on the safe use of tools and provided with safety instructions on the tool cards. The library will also have a designated area for storing safety equipment, such as PPE and first aid kits, to ensure users have access to necessary tools in case of emergencies.

### Final Three-Paragraph Kickoff Note

Welcome to Harborlight Tool Library! We are excited to introduce our new system for tool management. The intake label for tools is now teal, and safety reviews are conducted every Friday. Every high-risk tool requires two people for testing, ensuring safety protocols are followed. Additionally, we perform regular maintenance checks every six months, inspecting tools for wear and tear and making necessary repairs or replacements. Stay tuned for more updates and training sessions to ensure you are fully prepared to use our tools safely and efficiently.
